pr_title: fix branch flag on browse within dir
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->

Fixes #4666 

If there is no selector provided in `gh browse --branch my-branch`, we should open to the repos home with that branch selected, not the directory they are in.

issue_context.title: `gh browse --branch` doesn't open repo home
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

i just found this strange behavior under `gh 2.2.0`:

`gh browse` goes to the repo home no matter how deep i am in the repo directories, which is expected

however

`gh browse --branch <branch-name>` opens the current directory :thinking: 


### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Type this `gh browse --branch <branch-name>` in one of your repo's non-root directories
2. The browser goes to that directory

### Expected vs actual behavior

`gh browse --branch <branch-name>` should open repo's `<branch-name>` home page
comments:
@zachliu Thanks for reporting. Interesting that you expected that the `--branch` flag should start ignoring the current directory. I would have thought that with the `--branch` flag, exactly the same thing happens as without the branch flag, except that the git tree is opened at the specified branch instead of on the current branch. You would like it to be otherwise?

/cc @bchadwic https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/4007

wait... no you misunderstood, `--branch` does open at the specified branch but it goes to the current directory
if exact the same thing were to happen as without the branch flag, shouldn't it go to the home page of the specified branch?

Ah yes, I did misunderstand. Thanks for clearing that up.

Agreed that it's inconsistent that adding `--branch` to the invocation suddenly adds the current directory as well. That was probably an oversight. PRs welcome!

review_comments: Minor: let's generate this URL without a trailing slash, since that's GitHub web would also do it for branches but no path.

This is a great point and is the current behavior of using the branch flag even at the repo's root dir. As a new contributor on this repo, do we prefer to fix it here or create a new issue to track it properly?
Oh, if the old code also generated the trailing slash, then you're right that it should be changed in a PR separate from this one.  And even if it stays, it's not a big deal. 👍
